Every model has an `API` tab on its detail page with the exact input schema. Browse the catalog:
| `--input '<JSON>'` | Inline JSON body. Strings can contain newlines; quote-escape as needed |
| `--input-file <path>` | Read body from a file (JSON or YAML by extension) |
| `--output-dir <path>` | Where to download result files (default: cwd) |
| `--no-download` | Skip the download step; only print the result JSON |
| `--no-wait` | Submit and return `request_id` immediately; don't poll |
| `--timeout <seconds>` | Cap the polling wait. Default: model-dependent |
| `--output json` | Print machine-readable JSON for piping (default human-readable) |
| `--quiet` | Suppress progress, keep only the final result line |

content.user_title: Run RunComfy Models from the CLI
content.value_statement: Teams need a repeatable way to run RunComfy media models from scripts. This skill guides CLI install, authentication, model runs, polling, and downloads.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to install the RunComfy CLI with npm or npx.
Guides interactive login, token-based CI authentication, and account checks.
Shows how to run RunComfy model endpoints with inline or file inputs.
Covers synchronous polling, no-wait submission, status checks, and timeouts.
Describes JSON output, jq pipelines, batch prompt files, and retry loops.
Documents output downloads, output directories, and no-download mode.
limitations: Requires a working RunComfy account and valid authentication token.
Cannot run models that are unavailable in the RunComfy catalog.
Depends on the installed RunComfy CLI and network access to RunComfy services.
Does not validate model-specific input schemas beyond documented CLI guidance.

use_cases.title: Automate image generation
use_cases.description: Run text-to-image or image-edit jobs from repeatable terminal commands.

use_cases.title: Build media pipelines
use_cases.description: Submit video, lip-sync, face swap, or upscale jobs from scripts.

use_cases.title: Operate CI workflows
use_cases.description: Use token authentication, JSON output, and no-wait jobs in automation.

prompt_templates.title: Check my setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner verification before running a model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me verify that the RunComfy CLI is installed and that I am signed in.

prompt_templates.title: Run one model
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic model execution from the terminal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the RunComfy CLI command to run a text-to-image model with this prompt: [describe prompt].

prompt_templates.title: Create a batch workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a RunComfy CLI batch workflow that reads prompts from a file and stores each output separately.

prompt_templates.title: Automate async jobs
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced automation with polling and retries.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a RunComfy CLI automation plan that submits jobs without waiting, polls status later, and retries transient failures.

output_examples.input: Ask for a first RunComfy text-to-image command.
output_examples.output: A short terminal command, required input fields, and notes about where generated files are saved.

output_examples.input: Ask how to run many prompts from a file.
output_examples.output: A batch workflow description that builds valid inputs, creates separate output folders, and handles failures.

output_examples.input: Ask how to use RunComfy in CI.
output_examples.output: A CI-ready workflow outline using token authentication, JSON output, no-wait submission, and later status polling.

best_practices: Install the CLI through verified package managers and inspect any remote installer first.
Keep RunComfy tokens out of prompts, logs, repositories, and shared terminal history.
Use JSON output mode when scripting so downstream tools receive stable machine-readable results.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API tokens into chat prompts or generated command examples.
Do not pipe remote installer scripts into a shell without reviewing them first.
Do not enable web search or ingest third-party media unless the task explicitly needs it.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps an AI assistant use the RunComfy CLI for model runs, status checks, and output downloads.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need an account and either an interactive login or a valid RunComfy token.

faq.question: Can it run image and video models?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents image, video, editing, lip-sync, face swap, upscale, and related RunComfy endpoints.

faq.question: Where are generated files saved?
faq.answer: By default, downloads go to the current directory. The CLI also supports an output directory option.

faq.question: Is it suitable for automation?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers JSON output, no-wait jobs, status polling, timeout handling, and retry guidance.
